heading: Threat model
body: `bare-logger` is one of the addons Bare compiles into its binary, so every Bare process has it, sealed or not, and it inherits [Bare's threat model](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md). The module's own [threat model](https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-logger/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md), added in v2.0.5, says where it sits in that one. It writes to the standard output and standard error the process was given, which is how `console` writes in a default build, and opens nothing else. Whatever sealed code logs goes wherever those two go, so treat them as a way out of the process: sealed code can put any bytes into a file, pipe, or device log at the far end, and escape sequences into a terminal. That sealed code can write to them is not a bug. A memory bug in the C that formats strings and converts them to UTF-8, or any way to reach another file descriptor, is.
